en: The Sūtra of the Heart-Dhāraṇī of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìtōng of Dàzǒngchí Monastery during the Táng Dynasty.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Bhagavān was dwelling in the world of Sukhāvatī.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara went to where the Buddha was and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I possess the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of Sovereignty over the Mind according to One's Wishes."
It will be able to bring great benefit to all sentient beings of the future.
World-Honored One, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—
Those who uphold this dhāraṇī will swiftly achieve the gateways of samādhi and swiftly achieve the gateways of all dhāraṇīs.
It completely purifies the karmic obstacles of immeasurable and boundless worlds;
it accumulates immeasurable and boundless stores of merit and increases roots of goodness so that they can give rise to the spheres of immeasurable and boundless wisdom and supernormal powers.
They are able to transcend and enter the skillful means;
they excellently increase and bring to fulfillment the six pāramitās;
and they increase all the powers, fearlessnesses, and eighteen unique qualities of a bodhisattva.
The noble truths, the bases of supernormal power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path;
the attainment of meditative concentration, the liberations, the samādhis, and the samāpattis—
these enable those who behold them, as well as śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, to realize the stage of Buddhahood.
Through the power of the majesty of the wisdom they have cultivated,
they achieve intelligence, merit, and auspiciousness;
they apply themselves with diligent vigor to walking meditation.
Up to the attainment of the rank of a vidyādhara, endowed with eloquence, the power to soar through the air, the ability to become invisible, and mastery over mantras;
possessing all worldly pleasures, great wealth, and nobility;
and the accomplishment of the auspicious vase, the wish-fulfilling gem, and the *añjana* ointment.
It cures all illnesses and pains, completely dispels malevolent spirits, and eliminates calamities and epidemics.
It can accomplish all virtuous deeds and extinguish all karmic obstacles and hindrances.
He was well able to accomplish immeasurable and boundless dhāraṇīs and samādhis,
and had attained the most supreme and vast essentials of the Dharma.
He then spoke this dhāraṇī:

Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya | Mṛdusattvāya | Mahāsattvāya | Mahākāruṇikāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ tāre tāre ture | Ture ture ture | Svāhā || World-Honored One, this is the dharma of this dhāraṇī.

He is constantly worshipped, auspiciously praised, and prostrated to by all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, bhūtas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, rākṣasas, the seven luminaries, the bhūtadānavas, and the vināyakas.
Constantly for the sake of the Brahmās, the World-Protectors, and the hosts of sages,
may the sages who have accomplished this dhāraṇī offer worship,
rejoice, faithfully accept it, and bestow their empowerment.
They attain the purity of the holy life (*brahmacarya*),
and they are praised, revered, honored, and venerated;
all requisites for service are made fully available to them.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva further explained the method for receiving and upholding [this mantra]:
"If there be anyone who receives and upholds this dhāraṇī..."
One should bathe to become pure, don new and clean garments,
receive the vows, abide in a mind of loving-kindness,
and with a disposition of great compassion, employ truthful speech to eliminate greed and stinginess.
One should give rise to a mind that benefits all sentient beings,
a superior intention for their peace and happiness, and abandon all thoughts of anger and desire;
one should constantly recite [the mantra] without interruption.
Perform extensive offerings,
adorning the image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with scattered flowers, powdered incense, flower garlands, unguents, banners, flags, and precious canopies.
Before the image of the Bodhisattva, maintain a single-minded, firm, and resolute devotion with deep faith.
If one recites the Avalokiteśvara Tāre Svacittadhāraṇī one thousand and eight times every day without interruption until thirty thousand repetitions are completed,
all undertakings will be successfully accomplished.
Having accumulated merit, they will not be burned by fire or swept away by water;
no evil poisons can harm them. If they preach the Dharma for the fourfold assembly, [they shall be protected].
In all cases, one must burn incense and recite this mantra seven times.
This will cause whatever is spoken to be fluent and unobstructed, granting eloquence and fearlessness.
Furthermore, it will ensure that no harm can be inflicted by any celestial māras, non-Buddhists, or any malevolent spirits, curses, or incantations.
One's lifespan shall be extended and all aspirations shall be attained according to one's wishes.
A practitioner of mantras should act in this manner for each [deity] as previously described;
whenever entering the maṇḍala, one should do so before the image.
Sitting in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), perform the empowerment.
Form the fundamental lotus mudrā and recite the aforementioned mantra,
making offerings with a melodic *brahman* voice according to one's inclination.
The sounds are harmonious,
as if flowing forth from the mouth of the Honored One and entering the body of the practitioner.
In front of that seat, one should visualize a great lotus flower.
Above the flower, one should imagine the syllable *duḥ* (dru);
this syllable transforms into a blue lotus.
...until they transform into the Bodhisattva Multitude-Benefactor (Tārī),
adorned with various ornaments;
upon his jeweled crown is the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.
Holding a blue lotus against his heart with his left hand,
he grants all wishes and fearlessness with his right;
one should visualize him in this manner while reciting the mantra.
The syllables of that deity’s mantra revolve clockwise like a topknot within a pure moon,
appearing like crystal beads set in a bright mirror.
The light should penetrate both the exterior and interior with clarity.
The sound should be like that of a ringing bell, neither interrupted nor ceasing;
it should be neither too slow nor too fast, just enough for one to hear it oneself.
Regulate the breath and maintain a calm, composed, and careful mindfulness.
Once thirty hundred thousand recitations have been completed in this manner,
one will immediately achieve the fulfillment of all aspirations as desired.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appeared within a dream,
manifesting in the form of a bhikṣu, or a brāhmaṇa, or a boy, or a girl.
Sometimes they manifest in the body of a king, sometimes in the body of a minister,
or sometimes in the body of an elder, a householder, or others,
praising them by saying, "Excellent, excellent, Great Being!"
"You have already been able to uphold and protect the teachings of the Dharma.
Since your aspirations have been fulfilled, what further do you seek?
This is the aspiration required by the practitioner at this time."
One should explain this fully;
then one will attain the accomplishment of all auspicious fruits and rewards.
Regarding the second [section], the Dharmamudrā: First, the General Body-gathering Mudrā (Sarvasaṃgraha-kāyamudrā). With the two middle fingers, ring fingers, and little fingers of both hands...
Each hand crosses over toward the outside;
join the palms with the right pressing down upon the left,
and let the tips of the index fingers touch the backs of the palms.
Place the two thumbs side by side and upright so that their pads touch.
The mantra is as follows:
recite the preceding mantra seven times.
Whatever one performs according to the mind shall all be accomplished.
2. The Second Seal for Summoning: With the right hand, grasp the wrist of the left hand and extend it forward.
Move the four fingers of the left hand back and forth above the head.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvabodhisattvāya he he svāhā. Recite this mantra seven times while performing the mudrā and burning agallochum incense.
Please, O Bodhisattva, come immediately.
Hereafter, if one wishes to recite the heart-mantra of Tārā,
one must first perform this rite.
3. The Lotus Pedestal Seal (Padmāsana-mudrā). Third: Join the two hands together with the palms facing upward;
slightly bend each finger so that they take the shape of an opening lotus flower.
Then he recited the mantra: Oṃ sarvabuddhabodhi-svāhā. This is the mantra-seal.
It can cause immeasurable bodhisattvas to all assemble. 4.
The Fourth: Fragrance Seal (Gandhamudrā). With the thumb of the right hand, press against the tip of the ring finger.
The remaining three fingers are bent straight.
Then, place the left hand below it.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvabhyo bhūtagaṇebhyaḥ svāhā. This mantra-seal has the power to cause the eight classes of devas and nāgas to all come and offer worship.
5. The Fragrant Water Seal (Gandhodaka-mudrā), the fifth: With the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands, each grasp the thumb according to the method for forming a fist;
join the wrists.
Join the two index fingers together and recite the mantra:
Oṃ sarvotpātakāyarāja svāhā. This is the method for this mantra-seal.
Making offerings to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
6. The Mantra of the Body-Protection Seal (Kāyarakṣā-mudrā). Sixth: First, join the palms.
Bend the two little fingernails so that they face each other from behind.
Place the two thumbs against the two index fingers;
join the tips of the three fingers so they touch one another,
leaving a slight opening in the palm.
One should move the index fingers back and forth above the crown of the head. The mantra is:
Oṃ aritari tuttari turu hiraṇya-jāgare vīrakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvaduṣṭebhyaḥ sarvopadravebhyaḥ svāhā. Recite this mantra while performing this mudrā one hundred thousand times.
It subdues all sorcery and witchcraft;
it removes all demons, heretics, and their like so that they cannot cause harm,
and it serves to protect the body.
Furthermore, form this mudrā and recite the aforementioned heart-mantra before a stūpa containing relics.
With a sincere mind, confess all transgressions so that they may be extinguished. (7) The Mouth Mudrā Mantra: The seventh mouth mudrā is according to the previous heart mudrā.
Only change the two thumbs by bending them into the palms and pressing them together upon the joints of the two little fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ viśva gagana svāhā. Having performed this mantra-seal, when reciting the mantra aloud, one purifies the karmic obstacles of verbal actions.
8. The Seal and Mantra of the Great Repentance (Mahā-deśanā-mudrā-mantra), Eighth. First, with the right hand, press the tip of the middle finger’s nail with the thumb;
extend the remaining three fingers straight.
The left hand is likewise.
Press the thumbnail of the right hand upon the thumb of the left hand.
Place it directly before the heart.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvāya svāhā. With this mantra and mudrā, perform the confession.
It can eliminate all karmic obstructions and other transgressions, causing them all to be completely extinguished.
9. The Ninth Seal for Summoning All Mighty Ghosts, Spirits, Devas, Nāgas, and the Eight Divisions: With the right hand, press down upon the back of the left hand.
Interlace the four fingers of both hands with the tips pointing downward.
Move the four fingers of the right hand back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kuruḍa sarvadevāya svāhā. This is the tenth mantra for the great boundary-binding and the expulsion of Piṇāyakas, using the ring finger of the right hand.
Insert [the right hand] into the back of the ring finger of the left hand;
with the thumb of the right hand,
hook and grasp the little finger of the left hand.
Place it within the left palm,
pressing down upon the tips of the left index, middle, and ring fingers;
then touch the tip of the right index finger to the tip of the left little finger.
Press the thumb of the right hand upon the back of the middle finger of the left, and twist the right wrist.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvabhaiṣajyarasān pānta pānta dhāraya svāhā. 11. The Mantra of the随心印 (Sui-xin-yin; Heart-accordant Seal), the eleventh. Form the seal for the boundary-binding as previously described.
One should only change the index finger of the right hand so that it is approximately seven inches apart from the little finger of the left hand;
one who forms this mudrā...
By reciting the aforementioned随心真言 (Sui-xin zhen-yán), all wishes shall be attained.
12. The Seal for Entering the Path of the Indian Demon King Pāpīyān, Number Twelve: With the middle and ring fingers of the right hand.
Place the thumb joined together and bent within the palm;
straighten the remaining three fingers and extend the palm toward the chest.
The left hand is likewise;
it should be supported with the palm facing outward.
When forming this mudrā:
Pāpīyān led his retinue of followers;
they all aspired to enter the Way, prostrated at his feet,
and recited the original mantra of their true minds.
13. The Seal for Subduing the Six Heretical Teachers (The Thirteenth Seal for Subduing the Six Heretical Teachers).
This follows the previous seal, with the sole modification being that the thumbs are used to pinch the tips of the ring fingers and middle fingers.
When this mudrā is performed, the six teachers submit and are subdued;
one should also recite the original mantra. 14.
The Fourteenth: The Mantra and Mudrā for Purifying the Five Eyes of the Bodhisattva. Form the mudrā by joining the two thumbs and the two index fingers of both hands together.
The two middle fingers are held upright with their tips touching.
The two ring fingers press down upon the nails of the two little fingers.
The space between them should be placed against the forehead.

The mantra is: Oṃ sarvacaryādhārakāya svāhā. When this mantra-seal is performed, one shall behold the sentient beings of the six realms of existence as they become free from suffering and attain liberation.
15. The Amṛta-bestowing Mudrā, the fifteenth. With the left hand, join the index finger with the thumb;
extend the remaining three fingers straight upward, pointing outward.
Furthermore, with the right hand hanging downward,
extend the five fingers straight out.
This is the mudrā for bestowing ambrosia (*amṛta*).
May all sentient beings of the six realms be fully satiated and liberated.
One should also recite the root mantra.
16. The Sixteenth Seal for Averting Calamities: With the right thumb...
Extend the right ribs with the fingertips pointing backward;
clench the remaining four fingers into a fist.
Do the same with the left hand.
Extending the arms forward in anger,
having formed this mudrā,
the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvatruṭyā cchinda cchinda svāhā. (17) The seventeenth mantra of the Sovereign Seal (*īśvaramudrā*): Interlace the four fingers of the left and right hands in a reversed manner.
Furthermore, join the two index fingers together;
keep the two thumbs apart and extend them straight upward, holding them vertically.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvabuddhatrāya māraya svāhā. 18. The Eighteenth: The Samādhi Seal. Sit upright in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka).
Place the palm of the left hand over the back of the right hand and press them together at the heart;
recite the aforementioned Heart Mantra,
and one will immediately be able to enter the samādhi of the meditative absorption of cessation (nirodhasamāpatti).

19. The Seal for Summoning King Yama: The nineteenth seal for summoning King Yama is formed by hooking the two little fingers with their tips facing inward, pressing the right over the left, and bending the two middle fingers and two ring fingers.
Press each [thumb] upon the two index nails.
Hold the two index fingers upright, five inches apart,
and move the index fingers back and forth.

The mantra is: Oṃ sarvayamarājaṃ te piye svāhā. When performing this mantra-seal, if one wishes to know the number of the sinners, one asks for their names; the King himself then leads forth his various officials.
Coming from the void, they report to the practitioner. 20.

The Seal and Mantra for Summoning the Four Heavenly Kings. For the Seal and Mantra for Summoning the Four Heavenly Kings, number twenty: with the four fingers of both hands, interlace them in reverse.
Bend both thumbs into the palms so that the tips of the fingers are concealed;
move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvadevapūjā-hana svāhā. When this mudrā is performed, the Four Great Kings arrive simultaneously.
The practitioner asks about the affairs of the four continents and knows them all. 21.
The Seal of Pure Observance of the Precepts (Śīla-viśuddhi-mudrā), Number Twenty-one: With the right knee touching the ground.
Raising the head upward,
place the palms together at the heart;
then, with the two index fingers, press down upon the first joints of the backs of the middle fingers.
Place both thumbs against the sides of the two index fingers.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvapāpāni kṣayīkuru svāhā. When forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra:
All classes of sentient beings throughout immeasurable and boundless worlds shall attain the pure precepts. 22.

The Mantra of the Seal for Entering the Path While Remaining Invisible According to the Body (The Twenty-second Mantra of the Seal for Entering the Path While Remaining Invisible According to the Body). With the thumb of the right hand.
Press the ring finger and middle finger down;
extend the index and little fingers straight upward.
The left hand is likewise.
With the left thumb, starting from below and moving upward, insert it into the right palm;
hook and grasp the middle and ring fingers of the left hand,
with the right hand pressing down upon the left.

The mantra is: Oṃ kuru yati sarvakārya svāhā. This is the twenty-third seal for summoning the sages of the five realms of existence and others. To perform it, use the two middle fingers, ring fingers, and little fingers of both hands.
Form fists with both hands joined together;
place each thumb against the side of its respective middle finger,
and move the index fingers back and forth.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvakṛtājñākarmaprayogate svāhā. When forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [one should act].
All the ṛṣis were summoned and arrived.
He questioned them regarding their ṛṣi-practices, and they each related them in full detail. 24.
The Mantra of the Consecration Purification Seal. The Mantra of the Consecration Purification Seal, number twenty-four, follows the seal of the five paths as previously described.
In the superior [version], one merely changes the two index fingers so that each presses against the tip of a thumb,
with the two index fingers supporting one another.
Furthermore, with the two middle fingers held straight upright and their tips touching one another,
place them at the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ tijanpamudrā saṃjana svāhā. When constructing a great maṇḍala ritual arena, one should recite this mantra while forming this mudrā.
Through this consecration, boundless sentient beings all attain purity. 25.
The Seal for Water Dangers, the Twenty-fifth: With the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers of both hands...
Interlace the hands so that the right presses upon the left;
extend the two index fingers and the two little fingers straight upward with their tips touching one another;
bend the two thumbs and tuck them into the palms.
The mantra is: Oṃ udaka sarvadeva-udaka svāhā. By performing this mudrā and reciting this mantra, water cannot sweep one away, and all the devas will submit and take refuge.
26. The Fire-Disaster Seal (Agnibhaya-mudrā), Number Twenty-Six. This follows the previous Water Seal;
however, one only changes the two index fingers and the two little fingers, keeping each approximately one inch apart.
The mantra is the same as the aforementioned mantra for water-dangers;
it can cause fire not to burn and cause all devas to submit and take refuge.
27. The Mudrā for Wind-Dangers, the twenty-seventh: With the middle and ring fingers of the right hand.
Insert [the right hand] into the back of the left ring finger;
the two index fingers and the little fingers follow in accordingly,
pressing down upon the heart of the left ring finger and middle finger.
With the index and little fingers of the left hand,
press down upon the backs of the middle and ring fingers of the right hand;
extend both thumbs straight upward, keeping them at a distance from one another.
Turn the palms outward.
While performing this mudrā and reciting the *Uṣṇīṣavijaya-dhāraṇī*, [proceed as follows].
No calamities of wind can cause harm;
the kings of wind and rain spirits all submit and take refuge. 28.
The Celestial Seal (Devamudrā), the twenty-eighth: with the thumb of the right hand.
Press the second joint of the left index finger with the thumb of the left hand; then,
press the first joint of the right thumb with the thumb of the left hand.
With the remaining three fingers extended upright, touch the tips of the index fingers together,
keeping them about one inch apart.
Use the previously mentioned *cittānuparivartinī* mantra.
When forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, one will be able to see the events occurring in the Heaven of the Thirty-three. 29.
The Earth Mudrā (Dharaṇī-mudrā), the twenty-ninth, is identical to the preceding Heaven Mudrā.
Only change it so that the two ring fingers are used;
straighten and bend the tips of the index fingers so they touch each other.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ khaṭa paṅgaha siddhaye svāhā. When this mudrā and mantra are performed, all earth deities submit and take refuge.

30. The Seal and Mantra for Difficulties Caused by Bandits. Regarding the thirty-first [mantra], the seal and mantra for difficulties caused by bandits: with the index, middle, ring, and little fingers of the right hand, hook the four fingers of the left hand.
The two thumbs are each extended straight upward and separated.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvatusthapratuṣṭhanandaye svāhā. Form this mudrā and recite this mantra.
All dangers from thieves will be naturally bound so that they cannot cause harm.
31. The Seal for Dangers from Kings, Number Thirty-one. This follows the previous seal for dangers from thieves.
Simply change the right thumb to hook the left thumb; this is it.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvarājaduṣṭān svāhā. When this mudrā-rite is performed, all calamities involving kings, as well as calamities such as those of war and weapons, cannot cause harm.
32. The Abhaya-mudrā (Gesture of Fearlessness). Third and thirty-second: Standing upright, extend the left arm straight downward;
likewise, extend all five fingers downward.
With the backs of the palms facing backward;
the right hand is likewise,
with the palm facing forward.
The method for the mudrā of bestowing ambrosia (*amṛta*) is as follows. The mantra is:
*Tadyathā | ari duri dūri | hiraṇyagarbhe rakṣa rakṣa sarvabodhisattvānām bandhanaviye svāhā*. Recite this mantra while performing this mudrā one hundred thousand times.
All sentient beings shall attain fearlessness. 33.
The Mantra of the Seal for Warding off Poisonous Difficulties (Poison-warding Seal Mantra), Number Thirty-three: Interlace the four fingers of both hands with the backs facing each other.
Place the two thumbs touching each other with the palms turned outward.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ parākṣaya-yaṃ bhaṇḍa bhaṇḍa svāhā. If one enters a mountain valley while forming this mudrā, no venomous snakes, tigers, wolves, lions, or any other poisonous birds or beasts will be able to cause harm.
No poisons whatsoever shall be able to harm them. 34.
The Mantra for Seeking the Seal of Intelligence (Caturtriṃśa-tama-prajñā-mudrā-prārthana-mantra). With the two thumbs of both hands.
Twist each ring finger over the top of its own nail.
Extend both little fingers straight upward.
Bring the sides of the middle fingers together so that their tips touch.
Bend the two index fingers so that they each rest against the second phalanges of the two middle fingers;
the tips of the fingers should be about one inch apart.
Having formed this mudrā, place it directly before the heart.
One should also recite the随心 (Anupravr̥tta) mantra.
If there are those of dull faculties,
by forming this mudrā and making offerings while seeking a wish, they shall obtain their wish as desired.
In the past, there was an elder in the kingdom of Sphatika.
Although his family was very wealthy, he was by nature dull-witted.
His teacher performed a ritual of supplication according to the Dharma for seven days on his behalf.
Consequently, he attained clarity of mind and could recite a thousand verses daily.
Other manifestations of his realization cannot be fully recounted. 35.
The Seal for Destroying Hell (Bhūmi-narakabhañjana-mudrā), Number Thirty-Five: With the two middle fingers and the two ring fingers of both hands...
Bend each left palm so that the backs face one another;
the tips of the two thumbs, the index fingers, and the little fingers should each be separated by about half an inch.
While reciting the aforementioned root mantra, perform this mudrā.
The gates of hell opened, and the sentient beings suffering therein were all simultaneously liberated.
King Yama felt great joy in his heart.
This Dharma-seal was manifested by Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva out of his great kindness, great compassion, and pity for sentient beings.
36. The Seal for Seeking Rebirth in the Pure Land. Third and last: Join the palms at the heart;
place the two thumbs side by side, supporting them against the chest.
Recite the root mantra.
While forming this mudrā,
do so for the sake of all sentient beings.
At the time of death, form this mudrā and recite the mantra with single-minded concentration;
according to one's desire, one will be reborn in whichever Buddha-land one wishes to go.
37. The Mudrā for Saving All Beings Afflicted by Sickness and Suffering (Third-Seventh). With the two index fingers...
Hook the two middle fingers together with the right pressing over the left;
bend the two thumbs inside the palms;
and [place] the tips of the two ring fingers and little fingers [together].
Turn the palms inward and recite the aforementioned root mantra.
If there are sentient beings suffering from any kind of illness, [recite it for them].
By performing this seal-method, all the sickness and suffering of immeasurable sentient beings shall be entirely healed and cured. 38.
The Seal for Taking Treasures from the Earth, Number Thirty-Eight: With the four fingers of both hands.
Interlace the fingers of each hand in reverse within the palms;
join the two thumbs together pointing downward to touch the ground to discern the location where treasure lies.
Having formed this mudrā,
recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times.
Then the deity of the seven jewels will arrive all at once and answer whatever questions are asked.
39. The Seal for Seeking a Vision of Avalokiteśvara, Number Thirty-Nine: With the two ring fingers and little fingers, cross them respectively with the right over the left.
The two middle fingers are held straight and upright with their tips touching one another.
Each of the two index fingers is bent at the second and third joints so that the two nails face away from each other.
The two thumbs press down upon the joints of the two index fingers.
One should also recite the aforementioned root mantra.
Having formed this mudrā,
one should recite the mantra with a sincere heart, focusing the mind in right mindfulness.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will manifest his form.
Once the practitioner has seen him, they shall repent of all their transgressions and next seek to see the Buddha.
40. The Seal for Seeing the Buddha, Part Forty: Following the aforementioned seal, place it upon the upper part.
Change only this: bend the middle finger of the left hand and insert it into the space between the ring finger and the tip of the index finger of the right hand;
press the right middle finger over the back of the left middle finger.
The mantra is as follows:
*Tadyathā | ilidare svāhā*. If one forms this mudrā and recites this mantra one hundred thousand times, all the Buddhas of the ten directions [will appear].
When someone comes to ask the practitioner what they should do, [the master] then places his hand upon their head and bestows a prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*).
Master Tong’s commentary states:
Having been ill for twenty-one days,
he sought out this method of forming the mudrā; immediately,
he received the empowerment of a hand upon his head and was granted a prophecy.
This matter is never spoken of to others; one knows it only by oneself.
Thereafter, all dharmas will be accomplished.
Whenever this mudrā is performed, a wondrous fragrance and smoke invariably arrive.
If one can practice with single-minded sincerity, one shall attain Buddhahood;
this is inconceivable.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the city of Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and a great assembly of bodhisattvas. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara arose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said to the Buddha: "Blessed One, if there are sentient beings who hear this *Tārā-anupravr̥tta-citta-dhāraṇī*, they shall all be freed from all suffering and distress.
